profile.headline: Enterprise Systems Observability at Grainger
profile.summary:
I've spent nearly 20 years keeping enterprise systems running, and the last several building the tools that show how those systems behave.
I trained as a food engineer and started my career running a manufacturing business in Colombia. After moving to the U.S., I led an operations team, then spent seven years at Abbott Laboratories administering middleware: messaging, file transfer, data integration and workload automation.
At Grainger I've grown over 12 years from infrastructure administrator to software engineer on the Monitoring and Observability team. I build telemetry pipelines, alerting and AI tools across AppDynamics, Datadog, Splunk and Cribl for SAP, warehouse and infrastructure platforms.
Because I've run these systems myself, I know what good monitoring has to tell an operator at 2 a.m.: the real cause, not just the loudest symptom.
Lately I've been building AI into operations, including MCP servers, LLM agents for system health, and ways to test whether an AI actually uses its tools correctly.
Bilingual in English and Spanish.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.locationName: Lake Forest, Illinois, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
Software engineer on Grainger's Monitoring and Observability team. I build the telemetry pipelines, monitoring and alerting that engineering and operations teams use to run SAP, warehouse and infrastructure platforms across AWS and on-premises.
• Observability platforms: AppDynamics, Datadog, Splunk and Cribl. I design SAP application monitoring, health rules and dashboards, and route each alert to the team that owns the problem. 
• Telemetry pipelines: Cribl flows bring events and metrics from Zenoss, Splunk, Nutanix, Rubrik and third-party APIs into Datadog, Splunk and AppDynamics, with normalization and enrichment along the way. 
• Alert quality: I wrote the organization's alerting standard after reviewing hundreds of major-incident RCAs. I also built an alert-noise baseline showing that a single monitor produced 83% of all alerts. 
• Root-cause analysis: I led investigations into warehouse printing failures (4.4M connections analyzed) and slowness on handheld scanners. Both times I used data to rule out the network, database and infrastructure before naming the cause. 
• Observability rotation program: I designed and ran it, embedding with the Storage, Linux, Intel and SAP performance-testing teams. One result was a capacity and replication dashboard covering 29 backup clusters. 
• AI for operations: built MCP servers that give AI assistants access to monitoring data, and an LLM agent for SAP health reporting.
• Standards and research: standards for metric naming, metadata and credential management.

positions.title: Infrastructure Engineer
positions.description:
Administered and supported the infrastructure and application software behind Grainger's business: ERP modules and the applications built on them, middleware, standalone business applications, databases, infrastructure management tools and monitoring tools.
• Owned installation, configuration, upgrades, patching, tuning and troubleshooting across these products to meet service-level objectives. 
• Kept critical systems performing and available, including disaster recovery for critical components and processes. 
• Managed licensing and access, and kept the environment documented, sustainable and compliant with technology implementation standards.

positions.title: Infrastructure Software Administrator
positions.description:
• Installed, configured and deployed applications on Unix, Linux and Windows across multiple environments. 
• Managed and audited security access to meet SOX and PCI compliance requirements. 
• Designed and coordinated logging and alerting, which was the start of my work in monitoring and observability. 
• Maintained system documentation.

positions.title: Senior System Administrator
positions.description:
Owned the architecture and administration of Abbott's enterprise middleware, choosing and building the integration, messaging and file-transfer solutions that connected business systems.
• Messaging and file transfer: IBM WebSphere MQ and MQ Managed File Transfer, Accellion and Ipswitch WS_FTP Server for secure internal and partner exchange. 
• Data integration: Informatica PowerCenter. 
• Workload automation: CA Workload Automation AE (AutoSys) for enterprise batch scheduling. 
• Middleware monitoring: BMC Middleware Management, my first hands-on work in monitoring. 
• Gathered stakeholder requirements and planned the platform's future direction so the middleware kept up with business needs.

positions.title: Team Leader
positions.description: Led a team of call-center agents. I ran day-to-day operations against service goals, monitored call queues in real time, handled escalations, and trained agents on new standards and procedures.

positions.title: Painter
positions.description: Commercial and industrial painting on large-scale jobs.

positions.title: General Manager
positions.description: Ran an animal-feed manufacturing company, responsible for planning, operations, product development, marketing and sales. Kept the company a leading feed producer in southern Huila.
